7. Statement by director responsible for the business responsibility report, highlighting ESG related challenges, targets and achievements (listed entity has flexibility regarding the placement of this disclosure)

We have long recognized the importance of Environment, Social and Governance (ESG). We have worked upon bringing positive change, not just within the industry but also in the communities where we operate. We focus on waste recycling and run waste to wealth programmes to achieve 100% waste utilization. As the shift to a low-carbon economy is likely to unfold faster, the implications on steel sector shall be profound. We take cognisance of reduction in pollution to meet the evolving stakeholder expectations. We continue to seek innovative ways for this transition, through experimentation and investment. While the Company explores sustainable alternatives to traditional steel production methods, it is concurrently investing in new and efficient production methods. We also ensure to safeguard the flora and fauna in the course of our operations.

We endeavour to improve health and safety, and community well- being along with workforce diversity and inclusion. We follow high governance practices in our operations. We recognize the criticality of governance challenges relating to business ethics, ever-evolving compliance landscape, and the imperative of improved disclosures. To effectively mitigate these challenges, we have in place Code of Conduct for promoting transparency and accountability.
Our efforts towards ESG serves as a catalyst for our long-term success and resilience in the face of evolving market dynamics.

Details of improvements in environmental and Social impacts

The internal team continuously undertakes research and development (R&D) initiatives focused on optimizing power consumption, improving operational efficiency, and minimizing waste through effective utilization and recycling practices.
Reduction in environment pollution & Product carbon footprint, efficiency in production, reduction in water consumption.

The Company has obtained authorization under Plastic Waste Management Rules as an importer and complies with Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) requirements. The Company is regularly undertaking annual filings and ensuring compliance through authorized recyclers.

E-waste generated from IT equipment, electrical components, and instruments is collected separately and stored safely to prevent damage and contamination. The entire quantity of e-waste is handed over only to CPCB- authorized dismantlers/recyclers for environmentally sound recycling. Proper records and documentation are maintained for compliance.

Hazardous waste such as used oil, coal tar, contaminated containers, empty barrels, phenolic water, and spent ion exchange resin is managed in accordance with statutory requirements. The waste is stored in designated hazardous waste storage areas with proper labelling and safety measures. Used oil, coal tar, contaminated containers, and empty barrels are handed over to authorized recyclers for environmentally sound recycling. Spent ion exchange resin is disposed of through co-processing in the power plant as per guidelines of the Central Pollution Control Board. Phenolic water is utilized for quenching in the ABC of the Sponge Iron Plant at Siltara premises, in accordance with the SOP of the Central Pollution Control Board. The Company follows the manifest system and submits annual returns (Form 4) to ensure full regulatory compliance.

Other waste including fly ash, slag, and non-hazardous solid waste is effectively utilized or disposed of in an environmentally sustainable manner. Fly ash is supplied for cement manufacturing and brick making, while slag is used in brick plant. Domestic and biodegradable waste is managed through composting or municipal disposal systems.
